title: Retry coalescer and partial-response safety for hosted API during customer escalations
creator: Marcus Li
description: Summary: During the last two customer escalations we observed correlated 5xx/timeouts caused by aggressive client retries + edge-level fanout. This ticket implements a low-risk mitigation: a per-tenant retry coalescer (server-side soft-dedup) and a 'partial-response-safe-abort' path that returns an explicit abort/error when completing the request would introduce inconsistent partial outputs. Goals: 1) Stop retry amplification from generating repeated work on serving hosts, 2) Prevent clients from receiving mixed partial success payloads (e.g., streaming fragments + 5xx), and 3) Provide clear telemetry and optional per-tenant enforcement so we can roll out gradually to customers with ongoing escalations.
acceptance_criteria: Retry coalescer reduces duplicate inflight model invocations for identical idempotent requests within a 500ms coalescing window by >= 80% in canary region
Partial-response-safe-abort returns a consistent JSON error for streaming endpoints when in-flight kernel state indicates KV cache divergence could lead to corrupted outputs
New metrics emitted: inflight_coalesced_requests, coalescer_hits, partial_abort_count, coalescer_latency_ms
Canary rollout toggle available in console per-tenant with default off
No observable increase in end-to-end P99 latency for stable tenants outside of escalated cohort (< 3% change)
design_decisions: Coalescing only applies to idempotent generation requests (has idempotency_token or create_request_id) to avoid mutating workflows being collapsed
Server-side coalescer is best-effort with a short in-memory map keyed by sha256(request_canonicalized) + tenant_id; we avoid persistent locks to prevent contention during region failover

Partial-response-safe-abort triggers when a streaming connection has emitted >0 frames and the backend model host indicates cache mismatch or kernel-level OOM; clients receive a structured error with retry-after and a unique abort_id for debug
We will not change client-facing retry semantics yet; SDK guidance will be updated to respect abort_id and prefer exponential backoff. SDK changes handled in a follow-up ticket.
implementation_notes: Add lightweight in-memory coalescer component adjacent to frontdoor router (Rust) with sharded maps to bound GC cost
Integrate coalescer with existing request tracing; create trace span 'coalescer.lookup' and tag spans with coalescer_hit=true/false
Extend serving runtime to surface a stable 'kernel_state_fingerprint' for streaming sessions to decide if mid-stream continuation is safe
When partial-response-safe-abort fires, emit an assertive audit log to the tenant audit stream and include short diagnostic snapshot (last 3 frames, kernel fingerprints, host_id)
Create a console toggle and per-tenant rate-limit for coalescing (default 0 for new customers) and a forced-enable for escalation triage teams
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Coalescing may hide upstream failures from clients (they may see aggregated latency). Mitigation: coalescer will propagate earliest observed non-2xx error immediately and record the original timestamp for latency accounting
Risk: Memory pressure from tracking requests. Mitigation: add LRU eviction and a hard cap per router shard; instrumentation will alert when eviction rate > 0.1%
Risk: Partial aborts could be noisy. Mitigation: initial canary for 10 tenants with manual review and a throttled abort window (max 1 abort per tenant/minute)
Operational risk: debugging coalesced flows is harder. Mitigation: include coalescer.trace_id in all downstream logs and expose a debug endpoint to enumerate current coalesced keys for a tenant
rollback_plan: 1) Toggle per-tenant coalescer OFF in console -> immediate stop of server-side coalescing
2) Revert runtime partial-safe-abort via feature flag to always fallback to existing streaming behavior (safe default: return 5xx)
3) Hotfix to remove audit logging if log storm detected
4) Post-rollback: run targeted customer postmortem and tag commits for future rework
observability_changes: Dashboards: 'Coalescer Health' showing coalescer_hits, coalescer_misses, eviction_rate
Add tracing span 'partial_abort' and a dedicated long-term metric partial_abort_rate by tenant
Add SLO audit: incremental SLO for streaming consistency errors introduced by partial aborts
deploy_plan: Phase 1 (Canary): Deploy coalescer and kernel fingerprint in 'us-east-1a' with 10 escalated tenants enabled via console toggle; observe 72h
Phase 2 (Staged): Expand to all tenants with no history of recent escalations and run a 24h performance sweep
Phase 3 (Protective): Gradually enable for remaining tenants if metrics stable; set default to OFF for new accounts until SDK-level changes land
Migration window: 2 weeks with daily exec summary to oncall + escalation owners
comments: 2026-03-02 Marcus Li: Spike showed 87% duplicate invocations for a single customer burst — coalescer window tuned to 500ms cuts cost significantly in synthetic replay.
2026-03-04 Evelyn Park: Implemented initial in-memory map with tokio-based sharding; PR opened for review. Observed 1.8% eviction under synthetic load (within acceptable range).
2026-03-06 QA (Ravi S): Found race when a coalesced request experiences a backend retry which returns 202 then 5xx — added logic to prioritize earliest non-2xx and surface it to coalesced responses.

2026-03-08 Oncall (Hannah K): Canary tenant A reported a single partial_abort event that matched triggering conditions; attached logs and requested extended diagnostic snapshot (added to audit stream).
2026-03-10 Product (Lena M): Approved canary rollout but requested a conservative abort throttling of 1/min per tenant and explicit customer communication template for aborted streams.
